author: TEDx Talks
description:
The reality of surviving cancer can make celebrating survival a challenge. It can also be a tremendous opportunity to grow in confidence, resilience, and empathy. Through a series of handwritten notecards and journal entries, Nick discusses the valuable lessons he learned as a two-time cancer survivor and the importance of considering the relationship between mental and physical health.  

Nick is a dad, a college administrator, and a city councilor living in Brookings, South Dakota. He’s also a two-time cancer survivor. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How to relearn life as a cancer survivor | Nick Wendell | TEDxSioux Falls

We must take the helm of our digital lives, stay vigilant, and make conscious choices to protect our data and future. "Dr. Hermann Gumpp is the Managing Director of Enobyte GmbH, a Munich-based data protection and cybersecurity company, and serves as Special Advisor for Cybersecurity & Data Protection to the German-Japanese Business Association (DJW). He studied physics and computer science at LMU Munich, earned his PhD in biophysics, and spent many years as a Linux system administrator in the university’s computing center. Dr. Gumpp has worked in Japan as a consultant for large international corporation and at the
title: What people get wrong about cybersecurity | Hermann Gumpp | TEDxBerlin Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Como podemos falar em preservação da Amazônia se ignoramos a voz de quem vive nela? Nesta entrevista potente, conduzida pela comunicadora Mary Tupiassú, a grande Dona Onete despe a capa de artista para revelar sua alma de educadora e revolucionária.

Com a experiência de quem foi professora de História e secretária de Cultura antes da fama mundial, Dona Onete questiona o ensino tradicional, que muitas vezes apresenta uma “Amazônia errada” para as crianças. Ela defende que a verdadeira educação climática deve começar pelo olhar do caboclo — aquele que sabe que “cortar uma árvore é fazer a floresta sangrar” — e que o amazônida precisa retomar o protagonismo na defesa de seu território.

Uma conversa franca e necessária sobre identidade, a riqueza das terras indígenas e o orgulho “bairrista” de pertencer à floresta que sustenta o mundo. Dona Onete, natural de Cachoeira do Arari, no Pará, é uma das maiores representantes da música popular brasileira, conhecida como a diva do carimbó chame
title: Por que as escolas ensinam a Amazônia errada? | Dona Onete | TEDxAmazônia

By picking your people wisely, you create the foundation for fulfillment, resilience, and success in the digital age. With a law degree under her belt, Elsie quickly discovered that her true passion lay in entrepreneurship and human connection.

For over two decades, she has helped women around the world grow and scale their businesses with confidence. Affectionately known as the Queen of Networking, she believes that genuine relationships are the cornerstone of success.

title: Pick Your People: Why Your Network Shapes Your Entire Future | Elsie Borms | TEDxSurreyUniversity

description:
After a long career as a social studies teacher, Takahisa Kasai finally fulfilled his dream of moving to Kyiv, the capital of Ukraine. He bought a house with the intention of spending the rest of his life there, and was enjoying a peaceful life when a major historical event suddenly occurred, forcing him to return to his home country. He talks about the strength of will he felt from the people he met as the situation intensified.
　

『キーウ、戦争、そして「選ぶ意志」——移住者として見た現実』
　

社会科の教師として長年勤め、念願叶って葛西孝久が移住したのはウクライナの首都・キーウでした。骨を埋めるつもりで家を買い、穏やかな日々を過ごす最中、突然起こった歴史的な大事件に帰国を余儀なくされました。激化していく状況の中、出会ってきた人々から感じた意志の強さについて語ります。
　


 Born in Anjo in 1950. After graduating from Aichi University of Education in 1974, he worked as a teacher in Anjo. After retiring, he moved to Kyiv, and served as an external lecturer at the Department of Japanese and Comparative Culture, International Human Development of “Ukraine”. He also founded the international management company Natsu with the aim of sending Ukrainian talent
title: Kyiv, War, and the Will to Choose: An Immigrant’s Story | Takahisa Kasai | TEDxAnjo

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Indigo is a familiar color worldwide, but traditional dyeing methods are being lost. Mutsuko Sasaki encountered a unique dyeing technique passed down from Japan’s Edo period and was captivated by the depth of color it produced. As one of the few successors, she continues to carry on the tradition of indigo dyeing. Immerse yourself in the world of indigo as she speaks.

　
『藍染の秘密：藍が“命の色”である理由』
　

藍色は世界中に馴染みのある色ですが、昔ながらの染色法は失われつつあります。佐々木睦子は日本の江戸時代から伝わる唯一無二の染色法と出会い、そこで生み出される色の深さに魅了されます。数少ない継承者として、藍染をつなぐ彼女が語る藍色の世界に浸ってみてください。
　
経歴：
佐々木 睦子（ささき むつこ）｜藍染師

1977年、愛知県安城市出身。師事していた茶道と華道の先生が藍染作家だったこともあり、2012年に初めて工房で藍染を学ぶ。環境保全や心身の健康における藍染の関わりに可能性を感じ、2017年に徳島県の本藍染矢野工場にて、藍染師・矢野藍秀、藍遊両氏より、国選定阿波藍製造技術無形文化財・佐藤昭人氏のつくる蒅を使い、江戸時代から伝承され続けてきた「天然灰汁発酵建て」による本藍染の技術を学ぶ。ニューヨークで個展を開いたり、有松絞りの開祖の竹田嘉兵衛商店や、地元・安城市の「丈山苑」にて個展を開くなど、国内外で広く本藍染に触れる機会の創出に取り組む。
　
Born in Anjo in 1977. Since her tea ceremony and flower arrangement teacher was an indigo dye artist, she first studied indigo dyeing at a studio in 2012. Sensing the poten
title: Secrets of Indigo Dyeing: Why Indigo Is the "Color of Life" | Mutsuko Sasaki | TEDxAnjo

description: In a world that demands perfection and certainty, what happens when things fall apart? Breakdowns can become breakthroughs—not just for personal dreams, but in the stories we craft and the truths we conceal. Behind the polished surface of the news lies a reality shaped by pressure, chaos, and resilience. By challenging the clean and composed narratives we’re used to, this talk challenges the way we view failure, inviting us to embrace the cracks, the messiness, and the raw moments of life as the fertile ground where real transformation happens. Camar Haenda is a news anchor with a sharp instinct for storytelling and a calm authority on screen. Known for turning complex issues into clear, engaging narratives, Camar blends journalistic integrity with empathy—bringing stories to life while keeping truth and context at the core. Beyond the camera, Camar is driven by the belief that media is a powerful tool to inform, connect, and spark meaningful conversations. This talk was given at a TE

Rather than distant moon missions, he calls for policy, belief, and investment in using space technology to address real problems on the ground. Temidayo is the Founder and Managing Director of Space in Africa, the leading market intelligence firm shaping the future of the African space and satellite industry. With nearly a decade of experience, Temidayo is a trusted advisor to governments and commercial space entities across the industry value chain. Mrs. Sana Shams explores how artificial intelligence can support language diversity and digital inclusion. Drawing from her own experiences, she discusses building speech-based chatbots for citizen services and regional collaborations that made computing accessible in 11 local languages. Her talk highlights how AI, when used as a guiding tool rather than a replacement, can amplify unheard voices and support meaningful, people-centered innovation. Through real projects in Pakistan, she demonstrates how technology can be used to serve communities and promote inclusivity. Dr. Sana Shams is a Principal Manager Research at the Al-Khawarizmi Institute of Computer Science, University of Engineering and Technology, Lahore, where she leads the Centre for Language Engineering.

With over 20 years of experience, Dr. Shams has worked on numerous national and international projects focusing on natural language processing, technology development, and research commercialization for languages of Paki

Ultimately, the talk invites us to rethink human connection not as a soft ideal, but as a practical foundation for healthier minds, safer communities, and more resilient futures. title: Why Human Connection Is More Important Than Ever | Yves Clark Fabrigas | TEDxRizal Avenue

description:
What happens when women are taught to stay silent about their pain?

For an educator from Afghanistan and the founder of Lady Lord Academy, Kamila Afshar, healing became a powerful path — and self-acceptance became an act of resistance. Through her work with women and girls from Afghanistan, she noticed a repeated pattern: emotional exhaustion, hidden pain, and a deep feeling of unworthiness shaped by years of fear, restriction, and silence.

In this talk, Afshar introduces energy healing as a way to reconnect with emotions stored inside the body. She explains how unspoken feelings — such as fear, helplessness, and self-doubt — can quietly shape confidence, affect decision-making, and reduce the ability to move forward. Using both her personal experience and the stories of the women she has supported, she highlights how the Emotional Freedom Technique (EFT) can help people recognize, accept, and release emotional pain in a safe and gentle way.

title: When Healing Becomes Resistance | Kamila Afshar | TEDxDarulaman

Jack Jendo is an entrepreneur, digital transformation strategist, and UN Senior Fellow for Human Rights.
